name: Mythology trivia (medium)
description: 50 medium questions about myths and legends from cultures around the world. Written by Claude from cited web pages; every question names its page. Checked by a second model pass; the questions it flagged were corrected or left out.

source.name: Web pages cited on each question

items.question: In Hesiod's account, from which part of Zeus did the goddess Athena emerge?
items.explain: Hesiod says Athena came out of the head of Zeus himself. The thigh is where Dionysus was later carried.

items.question: In Hesiod's Theogony, Aphrodite rose from the foam that gathered around the severed remains of which god?
items.explain: Hesiod says Aphrodite was born from the foam around the severed parts of Uranus. Cronus was the son who did the cutting.

items.question: Which pair of Titans were the parents of Zeus, Poseidon, Hera, Demeter and Hestia?
items.explain: Hesiod's Theogony names Cronus and Rhea as the parents of the first generation of Olympians.

items.question: Dionysus was the son of Zeus and which mortal woman?
items.explain: Dionysus was the son of Zeus and the mortal Semele. Hesiod says both are now gods.

items.question: Why is Hades, brother of Zeus, not usually counted among the twelve Olympians?
answers: His realm was the underworld, far from Olympus
He was a Titan rather than a god
He was born after the Trojan War
He was banished from Greece by Zeus
items.correct: His realm was the underworld, far from Olympus
items.explain: Hades was a major god, but his domain was the underworld rather than Mount Olympus, so he is not normally listed among the twelve.

items.question: In Homer's Odyssey, which Olympian carries the message telling the nymph Calypso to release Odysseus?
items.explain: Hermes is the divine messenger and delivers the order to Calypso to let Odysseus go.

items.question: In Norse myth, who gave birth to Odin's eight-legged horse Sleipnir while in the shape of a mare?
items.explain: Sleipnir was born of Loki after the trickster took the form of a mare.

items.question: According to Norse myth, what did Odin give up in exchange for wisdom?
items.explain: Odin was imagined as a one-eyed old man who gave up his other eye in exchange for wisdom.

items.question: What were the names of the two ravens that brought Odin news of everything happening in the world?
items.explain: Odin learned of events through his two ravens, Hugin and Munin (Thought and Memory).

source.title: The Viking gods - National Museum of Denmark

items.question: Wednesday, or "Woden's day", is named after which Norse god?
items.explain: Odin is also called Woden or Wotan, and Wednesday takes its name from him.

items.question: In Norse myth, the goddess Idun looked after apples that kept the gods from doing what?
items.explain: Idun was entrusted with the apples that prevent the gods from growing old. The giant Thjazi once abducted her, and Loki brought her back.

source.title: Germanic religion and mythology - Loki - Britannica

items.question: Which pair were the first humans in Norse myth, made by Odin and his brothers Vili and Ve?
items.explain: Odin, Vili and Ve were said to have made the first human beings, Ask and Embla.

items.question: In Norse myth, Thor's hammer Mjollnir was among items the dwarves made as a penance after Loki cut off whose golden hair?
items.explain: Loki shaved Thor's wife Sif's hair while she slept. As a penance he had the dwarf craftsmen make magical items, including Mjollnir.

source.title: Norse gods, goddesses and giants you might not know - Routes North

items.question: In one Egyptian tradition, the loss and healing of Horus's left eye gave a mythical explanation for what?
items.explain: Horus's left eye was linked with the moon, so its loss and restoration explained the moon's phases.

items.question: In the Osiris myth, Set tricks his brother into lying in what, before it is cast into the Nile?
items.explain: Set had a chest made and trapped Osiris inside it, then cast it into the Nile.

source.title: Isis and the Search for Osiris (Egyptian myth) - EBSCO

items.question: Depictions of Isis nursing the infant Horus are believed to have influenced Christian images of which pair?
items.explain: Britannica notes that images of Isis with the infant Horus are believed to have influenced Christian imagery of Mary with the infant Jesus.

items.question: According to widely accepted Hindu tradition, which poet composed the Sanskrit epic the Ramayana?
items.explain: Tradition credits the poet Valmiki with composing the Ramayana. The Mahabharata is traditionally attributed to Vyasa.

items.question: In the Ramayana, how long is Prince Rama's exile from Ayodhya?
items.explain: Rama is forced into a 14-year exile with his wife Sita and half brother Lakshmana.

items.question: Which celebrated Hindu sacred text forms a part of the Mahabharata?
items.explain: The Bhagavadgita is a part of the Mahabharata and is highly regarded in Hinduism.

items.question: According to Aztec legend, Huitzilopochtli told his people to build Tenochtitlán where they found what sight?
answers: An eagle on a cactus holding a snake
A hummingbird drinking from a lake
A serpent coiled around a maize plant
items.correct: An eagle on a cactus holding a snake
items.explain: The war and sun god told the Aztecs to settle where an eagle perched on a prickly pear cactus held a snake.

items.question: Quetzalcóatl, the Feathered Serpent, was the Aztec god of what?
items.explain: Quetzalcóatl was one of the three great Aztec gods and presided over learning and the priesthood.

items.question: In Aztec myth, Coatlicue became pregnant with Huitzilopochtli after tucking what into her waistband?
items.explain: The myth says she found a ball of feathers, placed it in her waistband and so became pregnant with Huitzilopochtli.

items.question: In the Kojiki, from which part of Izanagi did the sun goddess Amaterasu emerge as he purified himself?
items.explain: Izanagi produced Amaterasu while purifying his left eye after his journey to the underworld. The storm god Susanoo came from his nose.

items.question: In the Kojiki, what caused the death of the creator goddess Izanami?
answers: Giving birth to the fire god
A fall from the Floating Bridge
A curse of the sun goddess
items.correct: Giving birth to the fire god
items.explain: One of Izanami's children was a fire god who fatally burned her at birth.

source.title: Amaterasu, the Mercurial Goddess of the Sun in Japanese Mythology - TheCollector

items.question: Which famous Shinto shrine is dedicated to Amaterasu as the highest national deity?
items.explain: Ise Shrine is dedicated to Amaterasu, the highest deity in Japanese mythology.

source.title: Amaterasu: The Japanese Sun Goddess - Nippon.com

items.question: The Irish hero Cú Chulainn was born with which name, before he took the place of a slain guard-dog?
items.explain: He was born Sétanta and was renamed "the hound of Culann" after taking the place of the guard-dog he killed.

source.title: Cú Chulainn: The Hound of Ulster - Irish Folklore

items.question: The name Tuatha Dé Danann is usually translated as the people of which goddess?
items.explain: Tuatha Dé Danann means "People of the Goddess Danu".

source.title: Celtic Mythology: Myths, Legends, Deities, Heroes - History Cooperative

items.question: In the Irish epic the Táin Bó Cúailnge, what does Queen Medb of Connacht invade Ulster to steal?
items.explain: The Táin is a cattle-raid epic in which Medb invades Ulster to take a great bull, and Cú Chulainn holds off her army.

source.title: Irish Mythology: The Complete Guide - Gods and Monsters

items.question: Which hero leads the warband at the centre of the Fenian Cycle of Irish mythology?
items.explain: The Fenian Cycle centres on Fionn mac Cumhaill and his warband. Cú Chulainn belongs to the Ulster Cycle.

items.question: In Roman legend, which god was the father of the twins Romulus and Remus?
items.explain: Rhea Silvia was impregnated by the war god Mars and gave birth to the twins.

items.question: The Trojan hero Aeneas, ancestor of Rome's founders in legend, was the son of which goddess?
items.explain: Aeneas's mother was Aphrodite, known to the Romans as Venus.

source.title: Romulus and Remus: The Legendary Founders of Rome - TheCollector

items.question: In the legend of Rome's founding, Remus settled on the Aventine Hill. On which hill did Romulus settle?
items.explain: Romulus settled on the Palatine Hill and Remus on the Aventine.

items.question: In the Babylonian creation epic Enuma Elish, Marduk forms the heavens and earth from the body of which slain figure?
items.explain: Marduk slays the chaos goddess Tiamat and uses her body to create the universe. Humankind is made from the blood of Kingu.

items.question: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, which flood survivor, granted immortality, does Gilgamesh seek out?
items.explain: After Enkidu dies, Gilgamesh quests for immortality and meets Utnapishtim, who survived the Flood and was made immortal.

items.question: In the Epic of Gilgamesh, which goddess sends the Bull of Heaven after Gilgamesh rejects her?
items.explain: When Gilgamesh spurns Ishtar, she sends the Bull of Heaven against him. The heroes kill it, and the gods then condemn Enkidu to die.

source.title: Mesopotamian Mythology: The Complete Guide - Gods and Monsters

items.question: In Journey to the West, the Monkey King Sun Wukong is born from what?
items.explain: Sun Wukong's story begins with his miraculous birth from a stone that produces a magical egg.

items.question: In Chinese creation myth, which cosmic giant breaks out of a cosmic egg and separates heaven from earth?
items.explain: Pangu emerged from primordial chaos, separated yin and yang, and raised the heavens while pressing down the earth.

items.question: Sun Wukong's weapon, the Ruyi Jingu Bang, is what kind of object?
items.explain: The Ruyi Jingu Bang is a magical staff that can shrink, expand or multiply at will.

items.question: In the Māori creation story, which son of Rangi and Papa finally pushed his parents apart?
items.explain: Tāne, god of the forests, argued for separating his parents rather than killing them. He pushed Rangi up into the sky and pressed Papa to the earth.

items.question: Which Māori demigod is credited with fishing up an island and stealing fire for humankind?
items.explain: Māui is the trickster demigod of Māori and wider Polynesian myth who fished up an island and obtained fire.

source.title: Māori Mythology: The Complete Guide - Gods and Monsters

items.question: According to Sir Thomas Malory, what does the name of King Arthur's sword Excalibur mean?
items.explain: Britannica notes that Malory said Excalibur means "cut-steel".

items.question: Which 12th-century French poet introduced the Holy Grail, and the love of Lancelot and Guinevere, into Arthurian legend?
items.explain: Chrétien de Troyes wrote five Arthurian romances and brought in the Grail and the Lancelot–Guinevere love story.

items.question: In Arthurian legend, King Arthur was the son of which king?
items.explain: According to the legend, Arthur was the son of King Uther Pendragon.

items.question: The Popol Vuh is a foundational sacred narrative of which people?
items.explain: The Popol Vuh is a foundational sacred narrative of the Kʼicheʼ people of Guatemala, from before the Spanish conquest.

items.question: According to the Popol Vuh, monkeys are all that remain of which failed attempt at creating humans?
items.explain: The Popol Vuh says monkeys are what is left of the wooden people, whom the gods rejected because they could not worship properly.

source.title: Mayan Creation Myth - University of Texas at Austin

items.question: In Inca myth, the creator god Viracocha rose from the waters of which lake?
items.explain: In the Inca creation story, Viracocha rose from the cold waters of Lake Titicaca into the darkness.

source.title: Incan Mythology: The Complete Guide - Gods and Monsters

items.question: In Slavic folklore, what does Baba Yaga ride when she flies through the forest?
items.explain: Baba Yaga flies in a mortar, and her hut stands on chicken legs.

source.title: Baba Yaga: The Slavic Witch of Russian and Polish Lore - Atlas Obscura

items.question: Which Slavic god was matched with the Roman god Jupiter in Lomonosov's 1755 Russian grammar?
items.explain: Lomonosov's 1755 grammar listed Slavic deities beside Roman equivalents and paired Perun with Jupiter.

source.title: Baba Yaga: The Slavic Witch of Russian and Polish Lore - Atlas Obscura

items.question: In a Navajo story, an impatient Coyote flung the remaining stars across the dark sky, creating what?
items.explain: While Black God carefully placed stars into constellations, Coyote grabbed the pouch and scattered the rest, forming the Milky Way.

source.title: Coyote: The Trickster Creator of Native American Myth - Gods and Monsters

items.question: Which creator-trickster of the Pacific Northwest is said to have brought the first people the sun, moon, fire and salmon, usually by stealing them?
items.explain: Raven is the Pacific Northwest creator-trickster who brought these gifts to the first people, usually by stealing them.

source.title: Native American Mythology: The Complete Guide - Gods and Monsters
